Thanks for the first round of feedback, @zcorpan and @noamr. New revisions are here.
 
Several areas of the spec ended up being relevant, mostly to consider the new `<poster>` element for sizes=auto and lazy loading (ie using the `<video>` as the intersecting/concrete box, inheritance of `loading` attribute for consistency between [poster] and `<poster>` lazy behavior).

General highlights:
- new `<poster>` element container (instead of the prior `posterfromimg` attribute) for opt-in
- Poster images retain img/picture responsive selection (including sizes="auto") using the rendered video’s concrete object width and lazy state, because the poster img is itself not rendered. Accordingly, the video element is used for lazy intersection observer. The line that mentions ignoring width and height on the poster img attempts to mention these 3 related concepts.
- `video.currentPoster` for consistent access to the poster url, regardless of where it comes from (attr or element)
- poster img, sizes, and lazy loading algos all needed touchups to consider the new element, particularly since the poster img is not rendered and needs to use the parent video for intersection and sizes. I borrowed "effective" to communicate the resolved eager/lazy state in a couple cases where it used to be directly obtained.
- For the waiting for `</video>` blocked-on-parser part, I didn't mention the preload scanner as I think that is implied to follow the same fetching rules as the regular parser, yes? 
- For a11y and alt, I removed the AAM-oriented language in the first round, but included a11y-specific examples and authoring guidelines for using alt in this context (to describe the poster frame, not the video as a whole). I have two HTML-AAM/ARIA external links in there but I'll need to make corresponding PRs for them.

Thank you!

Nice work @scottjehl!
See initial AI review: https://gist.github.com/noamr/52d96809f3ac3d444b0b5e5aa58a532c

Thanks @noamr - I think all of the points in the review are addressed now (I grouped the commits by topic), with these exceptions:

- **2.4.2 in your linked feedback ("What if `<poster>` is placed outside `<video>`?"):** I was thinking the `poster` element's _contexts in which this element can be used_ section covered that by saying it's only valid inside a `<video>` element. Do you think we should add an author note about it though? I suppose it's a little different than say, a `<dt>` outside of a `<dl>` because the `<poster>` element is hidden when inside a video, and won't be when outside of one. For now I assumed it's similar to other invalid placements and didn't need a mention.
- **Updated Web Platform Tests, AAM link:** we'll follow up with both of those soon.

Thanks

AI review # Review: whatwg/html#12585 — `` element for `video` **Author:** @scottjehl · **Fixes:** #10378 · **Touches:** `source` (+483/−79) **Status of support:** Mozilla is positive, WebKit has no position, Chromium has not been asked. WPT [#62290](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62290) is tentative. Implementation bugs, AAM/ARIA and MDN are not done yet. Line refs like `Lnnn` point into the PR diff ([pr12585.diff](file:///Users/nrosenthal/.gemini/chrome-ide/brain/f1b1100e-b0ff-47d5-9110-514b5b852001/scratch/pr12585.diff)). > [!NOTE] > I did not check out the PR or run `../build.sh` and the static-analysis scripts. Every finding below comes from reading the diff against the current `source`. --- ## 1. Status of earlier review feedback ### Inline threads | Thread | Point | Status | |---|---|---| | noamr r3442537596 | Make the light-tree/`descendant` semantics explicit | **Resolved / superseded.** The `poster image element` now uses child-only lookup (L658–675). | | zcorpan r4028497455 | Use a stricter child search (first `picture`/`img` child, then the `picture`'s first `img` child) | **Resolved** (L662–674). | | zcorpan r4028459144 | A11y mapping belongs in html-aam. Should the `alt` name the `video` instead? | **Partly resolved.** The normative a11y text was removed and the authoring guidance at L684–688 says to describe the poster, not the video. zcorpan's underlying question (accessible name of the `video` vs a separate `img` node) is still a design question for the AAM PR. The `#el-poster` links (L642–643) currently 404. | ### noamr's gist ([52d968…](https://gist.github.com/noamr/52d96809f3ac3d444b0b5e5aa58a532c)) | Gist item | Status in current head | |---|---| | 2.1 density-corrected natural dimensions | ✅ Fixed (L338–340) | | 2.2.1 stale resumption steps in update-the-image-data | ⚠️ **Partly fixed.** The new first step (L191–193) clears the steps but never unobserves. See B3. | | 2.2.2 no IO start in update-the-poster-frame | ✅ Fixed (L418–419) | | 2.2.3 `img` `loading`→eager doesn't unobserve the video | ✅ Fixed (L131–134) | | 2.3 redundant ancestor walk in effective lazy state | ✅ Fixed. It now uses `poster video` (L14–17). | | 2.4.1 vague "must be ignored" width/height | ✅ Fixed. It is now a note (L313–320). | | 2.4.2 `poster` outside `video` | ❓ Open. scottjehl asked whether a note is needed. See the answer in §5. | | 2.4.3 dev-edition boundary | ⚠️ **Regressed.** See B1. | | 3.1 `w-nodev` around algorithms | ⚠️ Applied too broadly. See B1. | | 3.2 redundant `data-x` | ✅ Fixed | | 3.3 `type` on `video` in examples | ✅ Fixed, including the pre-existing cases (L498–520) | | 3.4 missing *Fetch* label | ✅ Fixed (L427) | | 4 WPT out of sync | ❌ **Still open.** WPT #62290 was last updated on 2026-09-16, before the redesign. It contains no `` at all and still tests `posterfromimg`/`posterFromImg` (65 hits). | --- ## 2. Blocking / substantive ### B1. `poster image element` is defined inside `w-nodev` but used in author-facing prose The dfn sits inside `
` (L655–678). Text outside `w-nodev` still references it, so these become dangling links in the Developer's Edition: - the `poster video` dfn (L680–682) - the `alt` requirement (L684–688), which is an authoring conformance requirement - the notes at L313–320 and L491–495 **Fix:** move the `poster image element` `
` out of `w-nodev`. Alternatively, define it in prose for authors, e.g. "the first `img` child of the first `poster` child, or of that `poster`'s first `picture` child". The insertion, moving and removing steps can stay in `w-nodev`. ### B2. Parser-time ordering of `update the poster frame` and `blocked-on-parser` Two hooks now both run when an element is created, with no defined order between them: - L344–349: "when the element is created… update the poster frame" - the existing "when created by the parser, set `blocked-on-parser` to true" If the update runs first, the `poster` attribute is fetched immediately and then fetched again on pop. The pop hook is also a separate paragraph (L782–784) from the existing one that clears the flag (L778–780). Nothing says the flag is cleared *before* the poster frame is updated, and the early return at L370 depends on that ordering. **Fix:** - Merge the pop hook into the existing sentence: "…and set the element's blocked-on-parser flag to false, and then, if the element is a `video` element, update the poster frame for it." - Make the creation-time trigger explicitly not apply, or apply after the flag is set, for parser-created elements. ### B3. Lazy-load intersection observers can leak - **Case 1.** An `img` leaves its `poster` (or the `poster` is removed) while the `img` has pending lazy resumption steps. The new first step of update-the-image-data (L191–193) nulls those steps. But the `video` is still observed, and nothing calls *stop intersection-observing* for it. When it later intersects, the IO callback (L41–56) finds all three resumption-step slots null and `continue`s *before* the stop-observing step. Result: the `video` stays observed forever. - **Case 2.** A `poster` is inserted while the `poster` attribute's lazy steps are pending. `update the poster frame` nulls the poster lazy load resumption steps at L364 and returns at L382 without unobserving. - **Case 3.** The reverse also happens. The `img` was observing *itself*: it was created by script, its microtask ran before insertion, and it was later inserted into a `poster`. The `img` is never unobserved. **Fix:** when clearing resumption steps in these places, stop intersection-observing the element that was being observed, unless other resumption steps on that same target still need it. Alternatively, have the IO callback always stop observing when all three slots are null, instead of `continue`. Separately, it's unclear how L191–193 interacts with the *maybe omit events* flag and the `pending request`. Is nulling the `pending request` here intended to skip the abort-the-image-request step? ### B4. Compat/perf change for every parser-created `

> ### B4. Compat/perf change for every parser-created `<video poster>`
> 
> The `blocked-on-parser` early return (L370) defers the `poster` attribute fetch until the end tag of `video`. That changes behaviour for all existing content, not just pages that use `<poster>`. Today the fetch starts at element creation. Long fallback content, or a slow network mid-`<video>`, now delays the poster.

This was a known trade-off for switching to an element.

>  * This needs explicit implementer buy-in, especially from WebKit and Chromium, and WPT coverage.

Agreed.

>  * **Factual check on the note at L374–379:** I believe at least Chromium's preload scanner currently preloads `video[poster]`. Please verify before merging. If true, the note's claim that the speculative parser "only fetches what the normal parser would" means this PR also turns off an existing preload. That should be called out as an intentional trade-off.

Per spec it should be correct (assuming script doesn't change things before the real fetch). What it means for existing implementations could be one of:

* Turn off the speculative fetch for `<video poster>`
* Change the preload scanner implementation to "properly" speculatively fetch only the correct poster image when the `video` element is popped in the speculative parser.

Thanks @noamr and @zcorpan 

- Revisions are up based on the latest feedback. 
- Web Platform Tests are now updated to match - thx @alexgoff 
- Implementation Bugs are filed.

Still waiting to hear on WebKit's standards position, and a signal from Chromium as well.  Pending those, can this possibly advance to Stage 2?

AI review ## Specification Review: whatwg/html#12585 — Add the `poster` element ### 1. Summary & Process Status This PR introduces the `` child element for `

Thanks @zcorpan and @noamr. 
I believe the latest revisions address all of your feedback to-date. Like-changes are grouped in commits where that made sense.

A couple of notes:
- For the _maybe-stop-observing_ scenario of a video that is still being intersection-observed for an img that is no longer _the_ poster img (after moving it or removing it, etc), I took some liberty with the [algorithm name](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585/changes#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR8474) and wanted to flag it. I see other cases that use `maybe ...` and perhaps that'd be better? 
- [This addition](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585/changes/eee9c6baffad5345cd01d55f714754a9b5163f54) also felt worth calling out to make sure it's necessary, since it mostly cites examples of ways the preload scanner should match the regular parser, despite the spec already stating that it should.
- Decided to actually [gate the fetch of non-poster-image imgs inside poster ](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585/changes/3957fc050298068adbb6b251d7c4477ba3707007) 
- Lastly, I was torn over which redundant ALT usage language to downgrade to a note and decided the one in the images alt guidelines felt best for the canonical location. [Linked it up from `<poster>` while keeping the spirit of the guidance](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585/changes/bdcb00521cd4e1aa609b442a1fb0d4dac4754f15)

Looking forward to hearing how this all looks.

Hi @noamr @zcorpan, thanks for the feedback so far. I think we're up to date. Is this proposal ready for stage 3 at this point? We have multiple positive vendor interests, good test coverage, implementation tickets filed, a working chromium implementation, a11y tickets filed, and recent change requests seem to have settled into algorithm tweaks as opposed to any larger design changes. Thanks!
Moving to stage 2, let's discuss stage 3 in the next meeting.
